desc: Implement a Miller-Rabin primality test for numbers up to $10^{18}$.
Implement a function to find the prime factorization of $N$ (since $N \le 10^9$, trial division up to $\sqrt{N}$ is fast enough).

Implement a function to find an element $A$ of order $N$ modulo a prime $p$ where $N | p-1$. This involves computing $g^{(p-1)/N} \pmod p$ and checking if its order is $N$ by verifying $A^{N/q} \not\equiv 1 \pmod p$ for all prime factors $q$ of $N$.
For each test case $N$, iterate $k=1, 2, \dots$ to find a prime $p = kN+1 \le 10^{18}$.
Once such a prime $p$ is found, compute $A$ as described and output $A$ and $p$.
